Md Asaduzzaman with Mohammad Jamal Hossain, Advocates—For the Petitioner. (In all the writ petitions)

Mohammad Amirul Islam -------- Petitioner

Commissioner of Customs, Customs House, Chattogram and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
8. Mr Md Asaduzzaman, learned advo-cate appearing for the petitioner submits that the impugned demand imposing fresh liability under section 83 without issuing prior show cause notice and affording an opportunity of hearing is bad in law and liable to be cancelled. In this score, learned advocate referred to the case of Musa Bhuiyan (Md) vs Commissioner of Customs, Dhaka and others, reported 23 BLC 662 and an unreported judgment passed by this Division in writ petition No. 6009/2016 (Miah Mohammad Nooruddin vs Commissioner of Customs, Customs House, Chittagong and others). He next submits that admittedly the goods were finally assessed under Rule 5 of the Valuation Rules on the basis of data base value and the petitioner released the goods on payment of all duties and taxes as assessed finally by the customs authority as such subsequent assessment as stated in demand under section 83 invoking Rule 7 cannot be sustained in law inasmuch as under Rule 3(Kha) the respondent cannot jump and apply the detective method under Rule 7 in the process of assessment when the goods are already assessed under Rule 5 of the Valuation Rules. By referring Rule 7(1) learned advocate submits that this Rule provides that if it is not possible to assess under Rule 4, 5 and 6 then rule 7 can be applied but in the instant cases respondents themselves admitted that the goods were assessable under Rule 5 of the Valuation Rules on the basis of data base value as such fresh demand under section 83 invoking Rule 7 is liable to be declared without jurisdiction. Referring Rule 3 (kha) of the Valuation Rules learned Advocate submits that impugned demand is violative of the condition precedent of Rule 3(Kha) inasmuch as Rule 3(Kha) provides that Rule 7 is applicable only when the importer file an application to apply Rule 7 with approval of the Commissioner of Customs. In this score, learned advocate referred to the case of Amirul Islam (Md) vs Commissioner of Customs and others, reported in 18 BLC 7 and an unreported judgment passed by this Division in Customs Appeal No. 75 of 2013 (Procter and Gamble Bangladesh (Private) Limited. vs Customs, Excise and VAT Appellate Tribunal). He again submits that section 83B of the Customs Act barred fresh imposition of liability under section 83A after expiry of 3(three) years from the date on which original assessment was made and, as such, impugned notice under section 83A in writ petition Nos. 6990 of 2016 and 7006 of 2016 are barred by limitation. 

 12. From the submissions made by the learned advocate for the petitioner and learned Deputy Attorney-General it appears that points of law involve in these writ petitions are: a) whether show cause notice is mandatory before making the demand under section 83A of the Customs Act? b) whether Rule 7 of the Valuation Rules can be applied abruptly for making subsequent demand under section 83A of the Customs Act on the goods already assessed finally and released following the provision of Rule 5 of the Valuation Rules? c) whether Rule 7 of the Valuations Rules can be applied directly without adopting sequential method as per terms of rule 3(Ka) of the Valuation Rules? d) whether the demands are barred by limitation? e) whether writ petitions are maintainable without exhausting forum of appeal?
